newsitem.title: INDIA: Three Hindu bus passengers shot dead in Kashmir.
newsitem.headline: Three Hindu bus passengers shot dead in Kashmir.

text.p: Three Hindu bus passengers were shot dead by suspected separatist rebels in the northern Indian state of Jammu and Kashmir, police said on Monday.
They said armed rebels, believed to be Moslems, stopped a bus carrying 32 people late on Sunday and forced all six Hindu passengers aboard to alight.

When the guerrillas told the passengers to walk about 100 yards (metres) away from the bus, one escaped. The rebels released two others and gunned down three, who were high school teachers, police said.
The killings occurred near the village of Gool Gulab Garh, some 180 km (110 miles) northeast of Jammu, the winter capital of Jammu and Kashmir, mostly Hindu India's only Moslem-majority state.

Police and hospitals say more than 20,000 people have been killed in the region since a separatist insurgency broke out in 1990. More than a dozen rebel groups are fighting for merger with neighbouring Islamic Pakistan or an independent homeland.
Most Hindus fled the Kashmir Valley seven years ago fearing retaliation after the Indian army opened fire against separatist demonstrators.
Rebels killed 15 Hindu bus passengers in a similar attack in 1993 on August 14, Pakistan's independence day.
India has repeatedly accused Pakistan of arming and training the insurgents. Islamabad says it provides only moral and diplomatic support to the rebels.
